rationale: Resolve the accepted census identity Digital Generation (d/b/a Takanock) to the existing canonical Takanock, LLC production and evaluated-seed record rather than creating a duplicate. ArcLight's 2025 ESG report expressly supplies the DBA relationship. Takanock's SEC Form D establishes the legal issuer, Traverse City principal office and April 30, 2025 first equity sale. In sworn December 2025 testimony, Takanock's CEO stated that ArcLight and DigitalBridge became the company's collective majority owners in the April financing while original investors retained a minority interest. Add DigitalBridge as a separately displayed current co-owner, retain ArcLight, and state the disclosed collective-majority position without inventing an individual sponsor percentage, fund, or legal vehicle. No company-level sale, realization or pending exit was identified through August 13, 2026.

beforeImage.name: Takanock, LLC
beforeImage.description: Takanock develops and finances digital and power infrastructure solutions for data centers in power-constrained markets. The platform serves hyperscale and other large data center demand through an asset-heavy model tied to power delivery, infrastructure deployment, and site enablement rather than retail colocation. Public disclosures state that Takanock secured $500 million of capital from ArcLight and DigitalBridge in June 2025 and identified the company as being based in Traverse City, Michigan. The business is designed to address the power and infrastructure bottlenecks associated with rapid data center expansion. ArcLight and DigitalBridge announced the capital commitment in June 2025, while public sources do not disclose the ownership percentages within Takanock.

milestones.event: The transaction positioned Takanock to pursue deployments in power-constrained data center markets.
Takanock announced a $500 million capital commitment from ArcLight and DigitalBridge.

afterImage.name: Takanock, LLC
afterImage.description: Takanock, LLC develops power-enabled sites and permanent on-site generation for data centers in power-constrained U.S. markets. The Traverse City-based platform combines land, entitlements, generation, fuel supply and grid interconnection to accelerate time to power for hyperscale and other large data-center customers, with disclosed activity including Northern Virginia and Phoenix. The operating business was formed in 2023 and reorganized under the current Delaware LLC in 2025. ArcLight and DigitalBridge became collective majority owners in an April 2025 equity financing and announced aggregate commitments of up to US$500 million on June 25, 2025; original investors retained a collective minority interest. Each sponsor's individual percentage, ArcLight fund and exact joint investment vehicle are not publicly disclosed.
